description: This file appears to be documentation content (in Markdown format) describing the 'Clock' class and its methods in a software project. It explains how to simulate and control time-related behaviors in tests, including methods like fastForward, install, runFor, pauseAt, resume, setFixedTime, and setSystemTime. The content includes usage examples in multiple programming languages, method parameters, and versioning details.

classes.name: Clock
classes.description: A utility class for mocking and controlling time in tests, including methods to fast-forward, install fake timers, run for a duration, pause at a specific time, set fixed system time, and set system time without affecting timers.

methods.name: Clock.fastForward
methods.description: Advances the clock by a specified amount of time, triggering due timers at most once.

methods.name: Clock.install
methods.description: Installs fake implementations for time-related functions, allowing manual control of the flow of time during tests.

methods.name: Clock.runFor
methods.description: Advances the clock and fires all relevant timers for the specified duration.

methods.name: Clock.pauseAt
methods.description: Advances the clock to a specified time and pauses further time progression, pausing timers.

methods.name: Clock.resume
methods.description: Resumes the flow of time, allowing timers to fire normally.

methods.name: Clock.setFixedTime
methods.description: Sets the current time to a fixed value, making Date.now and new Date() return this fixed time.

methods.name: Clock.setSystemTime
methods.description: Changes the system time for the page without affecting timers, useful for simulating system time shifts.
